facts: Video provides rich visual cues such as motion and appearance.
Video provides long-range temporal interactions among objects.
The authors aim to capture long-range temporal interactions among objects.
The authors aim to construct a powerful intermediate-level video representation for subsequent recognition.
The authors seek to obtain spatio-temporal over-segmentation of a video into regions that respect object boundaries.
The authors seek to associate object pixels over many video frames.
The contributions of the paper are twofold.
The authors develop an efficient spatio-temporal video segmentation algorithm.
The spatio-temporal video segmentation algorithm incorporates long-range motion cues from the past frames.
The spatio-temporal video segmentation algorithm incorporates long-range motion cues from the future frames.
The long-range motion cues are in the form of clusters of point tracks with coherent motion.
The authors devise a new track clustering cost function.
The track clustering cost function includes occlusion reasoning in the form of depth ordering constraints.
The track clustering cost function includes motion similarity along the tracks.
The authors evaluate the proposed approach on a challenging set of video sequences of office scenes from feature length movies.
